name: Campaign Monitor
description: Track marketing campaign performance, budget pacing and channel health from daily performance snapshots
backend_requirements: Access control: anyone may read campaigns, their performance and the public summaries; require auth for creating and updating campaigns and for recording performance, and only a campaign's owner may change it; admin endpoints are restricted to the admin account
Campaigns: any signed-in user may create one and becomes its owner; PATCH /api/campaigns/:id and POST /api/campaigns/:id/performance by anyone else answer 403

Campaign validation: name is a required non-empty string of at most 120 characters; channel is one of search, social, email, video; daily_budget is a number above 0 and at most 1000000; conversion_goal, when given, is a whole number of at least 1; launch_at is a required ISO 8601 date-time; end_at, when given, is not before launch_at; notes, when given, is at most 2000 characters

Status: a new campaign starts as draft; PATCH may move draft to active, active to paused, paused to active, and active or paused to completed; setting the current status again is allowed, any other change answers 409, and a completed campaign accepts no further changes (409)

Performance snapshots: POST /api/campaigns/:id/performance records one day's impressions, clicks, conversions, revenue and spend; all are zero or more, clicks may not exceed impressions and conversions may not exceed clicks (400); posting a date that already has a snapshot replaces it (200), a new date answers 201

Computed fields on every campaign: spend_to_date and conversions are the sums over its snapshots; planned_spend is daily_budget times the number of snapshot days; pacing is spend_to_date divided by planned_spend rounded to two decimals (null without snapshots); pacing_status is 'over' when pacing is above 1.10, 'under' when it is below 0.90, 'on_track' otherwise and 'no_data' without snapshots

GET /api/campaigns returns active campaigns; ?query= matches the name case-insensitively, ?status=, ?channel= and ?owner= (the owner's username) filter exactly, ?pacing_status= keeps one pacing status, ?sort= is one of -created_at (default), launch_at, -launch_at, name, -spend_to_date, -updated_at, ?page= and ?page_size= page the result (page_size default 20, at most 100), and total counts every matching campaign

GET /api/campaigns/:id/performance returns the campaign's snapshots by date (oldest first), their totals, click-through rate (clicks / impressions), conversion rate (conversions / clicks) and cost per conversion (spend / conversions), each rounded to four decimals and null when the divisor is 0, plus alerts: one overspend_day alert for each snapshot whose spend is above daily_budget, and one pacing_over or pacing_under alert when pacing_status is over or under

GET /api/public/stats summarises active campaigns: counts by status, total spend, total conversions, total revenue and the number of over-pacing campaigns; GET /api/public/featured returns up to three active campaigns with status active and the most conversions, ties broken by the newer campaign
Deactivated campaigns (is_active false) are left out of every public list and summary and answer 404 on the public campaign endpoints; the admin overview still lists them; campaigns are never deleted

Errors answer with a JSON object {"detail": "<message>"}: 400 for invalid input, 401 without a valid token, 403 for a non-owner or a non-admin, 404 for unknown ids, 409 for a status change that is not allowed
frontend_requirements: Everyone sees the landing page, the campaign browser and campaign details read-only; signed-in users also get the create form, their dashboard and, on their own campaigns, the edit, status and record-performance controls, and visitors see a 'Sign in to manage campaigns' prompt in their place
Sign-in and registration forms that call /api/auth/login and /api/auth/register; keep the token for later requests, show the signed-in username and offer sign-out
Landing page: summary cards from /api/public/stats (active campaigns, total spend, conversions, revenue, over-pacing count) and cards for the featured campaigns

Campaign browser: a table with name, channel, status, owner, daily budget, spend to date and a pacing badge; a name search, status chips, channel and pacing filters, sort controls and previous/next paging

Campaign detail: key figures (spend to date against planned spend, conversions against conversion_goal, click-through and conversion rates, cost per conversion), a chart of daily spend and conversions, a table of the snapshots and the alerts as warning badges
Owner dashboard: the signed-in user's campaigns (?owner= with their username), over-pacing campaigns first, then the most recently updated (?sort=-updated_at), with their alerts
Create and edit forms and a record-performance form for one day's figures, each showing the API's validation messages next to the form; status buttons offer only the changes the current status allows
admin_requirements: Admin overview: every campaign, active or not, with total, active and inactive counts, the number of paused and over-pacing campaigns and the conversions recorded for the last seven days
Review queue: the overview filtered to paused or over-pacing campaigns (?status=paused, ?pacing_status=over)
Toggle a campaign's active status from the overview to take it out of the public views

api_endpoints.description: Create a campaign owned by the signed-in user (status draft)
List active campaigns, searched, filtered, sorted and paged

query.query: Case-insensitive text matched against the name
query.status: One of draft, active, paused, completed
query.channel: One of search, social, email, video
query.pacing_status: One of over, under, on_track, no_data

api_endpoints.description: One active campaign with its computed fields
Change some of a campaign's fields or its status (owner only); omitted fields keep their values
Daily snapshots, totals, rates and pacing alerts of an active campaign

alerts.message: Spend 131.50 is above the daily budget of 120.00

api_endpoints.description: Record or replace one day's snapshot (owner only)
Up to three running campaigns with the most conversions

data_models.name: Campaign
data_models.description: A marketing campaign; spend_to_date, conversions, planned_spend, pacing and pacing_status are computed from its snapshots

fields.name: string (required, max 120 chars)
fields.channel: string (one of: search, social, email, video)
fields.status: string (one of: draft, active, paused, completed; default draft)
fields.owner_id: integer (references the signed-in user who created it; shown as the owner's username)
fields.updated_at: datetime (auto, changes on every update and every recorded snapshot)
fields.is_active: boolean (default true; false hides the campaign from public endpoints and summaries)

data_models.name: PerformanceSnapshot
data_models.description: One campaign's figures for one day

fields.campaign_id: integer (references Campaign.id; one snapshot per campaign and date)

admin_api_endpoints.description: Admin overview: every campaign with counts and risk metrics

query.status: One of draft, active, paused, completed
query.pacing_status: One of over, under, on_track, no_data
